rows.en: “And you’re wearing your own clothes again.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And yet you came to school in normal clothes again?"

rows.jp: 群青に校則はあってなきに等しい。
rows.en: At Gunjo, the school rules might as well not have existed.

ghs.en: School regulations in Gunjou are next to ignorable.

rows.jp: なにか差し障りがあれば、警備員の出番だ。
rows.en: If anything caused trouble, the guards stepped in.

ghs.en: If a problem arises, the guards intervene.

rows.jp: 学生が自らを律する必要などない。
rows.en: There was no need for students to govern themselves.

ghs.en: There is no need for students to regulate, judge, or decide for themselves.
ghs.assessment: 自らを律する means students disciplining themselves. 'Regulate, judge, or decide for themselves' adds two unrelated activities.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There is no need for students to discipline themselves.'

highlights.text: There is no need for students to regulate, judge, or decide for themselves.

rows.jp: だから制服着用という決まり事は、まるで意味をなさない。
rows.en: That rendered the rule requiring uniforms entirely meaningless.

ghs.en: Therefore, the regulatory standard mandating the use of uniforms is entirely ignorable.
ghs.assessment: The uniform rule is said to have no meaning at all. 'Entirely ignorable' instead says a meaningful rule exists but can be disregarded.
ghs.remedy: Use 'So the rule requiring uniforms is completely meaningless.'

highlights.text: Therefore, the regulatory standard mandating the use of uniforms is entirely ignorable.

rows.jp: いかに天下群青とはいえ、年頃の少女をひんむいて制服に着替えさせるわけにはいかないからだ。
rows.en: Even mighty Gunjo could hardly strip a young woman naked and force her into one.

ghs.en: In this lone Gunjou under the heavens, to force a girl of that age back into the uniform she took off is hopeless beyond all effort.
ghs.assessment: Even at Gunjou they cannot strip a teenage girl and force her into uniform. The English invents a uniform she previously took off and calls the task hopeless rather than impermissible.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even at freewheeling Gunjou, they can't strip a teenage girl and force her into uniform.'

highlights.text: In this lone Gunjou under the heavens, to force a girl of that age back into the uniform she took off is hopeless beyond all effort.

rows.jp: 他の者と自らを分断するための。
rows.en: It was a way for Touko to cut herself off from everyone else.

ghs.en: She does it to cut herself off from other people.

rows.jp: それは冬子の確固とした抵抗に違いなかった。
rows.en: That had to be Touko’s unwavering act of resistance.

ghs.en: That was Touko's unshakable, unmistakable resistance.

rows.jp: 「萌え萌え制服姿が見たいにゃー」
rows.en: “I wanna see you all cute-cute in your uniform, meow.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I wannya see you in moe-moe uniform clothes, nya～n!"

ghs.assessment: うーん is a thoughtful or doubtful hum. 'Yep' turns it into agreement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hmm.'

highlights.text: Yee-ep.

rows.jp: こうまで無視が似合うキャラも珍しい。
rows.en: Few characters wore indifference as naturally as she did.

ghs.en: A character that looks so good while ignoring this much is rare.

rows.jp: 冬子はこんな状態でいるのが、もっとも絵になるわけで。
rows.en: Touko was at her most picturesque in exactly this state.

ghs.en: The more Touko stays just like this, the more like a picture she becomes.
ghs.assessment: The source says Touko is most picturesque in this state. 'The more she stays ... the more' invents a progressive comparative relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Touko is at her most picturesque like this.'

highlights.text: The more Touko stays just like this, the more like a picture she becomes.

rows.jp: 俺は隣に座って、じっと横顔を見つめた。
rows.en: I sat beside her and stared intently at her profile.

ghs.en: I sat her neighbor, and motionlessly gazed at her profile.
ghs.assessment: The source says he sits beside her. 'I sat her neighbor' is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I sat beside her and gazed steadily at her profile.'

highlights.text: I sat her neighbor, and motionlessly gazed at her profile.

rows.en: I could have stared forever without tiring of it.

ghs.assessment: The source says she bristled or became furious. 'The rage shoots upwards' is an unnatural literal image and shifts to present.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She bristled.'

highlights.text: The rage shoots upwards.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come on, paintings should not be talking."
Touko: "I don't get you at all!"

rows.jp: 「おまえは語尾が～だわ、とか～ですわ、とかオバサン臭いんだからあんま喋るなよイメージが崩れる」
rows.en: “Your sentence endings are all ‘I declare’ and ‘indeed,’ like some old lady. Better not talk too much—you’ll ruin the image.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You always drop in affectations like 'shan't' or 'mayhap' that stink of grandmother, so don't talk too much or your image will crumble."

ghs.assessment: 'WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID' is not grammatical English and does not form the intended slurred 'What did you say?!'
ghs.remedy: Use a distorted but intelligible 'WHAAAT DID YOU SAAAAY?!'

highlights.text: Touko: "WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID?!?"

ghs.assessment: ダメだこりゃ means 'this is hopeless/no good.' 'It's dead' assigns literal death instead.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This is hopeless.'

highlights.text: It's deeead.

rows.jp: ぬぁんですってーとか言い出したよ。
rows.en: And now she was saying things like “I beg your paaardon?”

ghs.assessment: The narration quotes her distorted 'What did you say?' The embedded 'whas'd you said' is ungrammatical beyond the source's phonetic distortion.
ghs.remedy: Use an intelligible distorted form of 'what did you say.'

highlights.text: She actually uttered "whas'd you said".

ghs.en: This is the demise of a work of fine arts.

rows.jp: 世界正義という強圧的な概念とともにキレイさっぱり根絶されたであろう米国人のように、肩をすくめてみせた。
rows.en: I shrugged like an American—one of those people presumably wiped from the earth along with the domineering idea of global justice.

ghs.en: I made display of a shrug similar to that of an American that fears himself thoroughly eradicated alongside the coercive concept known as the righteousness of the world.
ghs.assessment: The source compares his shrug to an American who would have been eradicated along with coercive 'world justice.' The English says the American merely fears his own eradication and is syntactically tangled.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I shrugged like an American who would have been wiped out along with the coercive idea of world justice.'

highlights.text: I made display of a shrug similar to that of an American that fears himself thoroughly eradicated alongside the coercive concept known as the righteousness of the world.

rows.jp: 「おまえに芸術の破壊者という二つ名を与える」
rows.en: “I hereby bestow upon you the epithet Destroyer of Art.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I bestow you the second name of, Destroyer of Arts."
ghs.assessment: 二つ名 means an epithet or sobriquet, not a literal second name. 'Bestow you' also lacks the required preposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I bestow on you the epithet Destroyer of Art.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I bestow you the second name of, Destroyer of Arts."

rows.jp: 「よかったな。ピカソもそんなこと言われてたぞ。またすごいのとならんだな」
rows.en: “Good for you. Picasso got called that too. Once again, you’re keeping impressive company.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's to be happy, too. Picasso himself was called the same. No finer thing on the same level as it."
ghs.assessment: The source says Picasso was called the same thing and congratulates her on joining another great figure. The English is syntactically incoherent and does not express the comparison.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Good for you. Picasso was called that too. You're in distinguished company again.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's to be happy, too. Picasso himself was called the same. No finer thing on the same level as it."

ghs.assessment: The recurring archaic-English adaptation is valid, but this middle link has a grammatical and prepositional shift.
ghs.remedy: Keep the archaic callback mechanism while repairing the relation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Giving a fright shan't we～!"

rows.jp: 「ですわなんて言ってないでしょっ！！」

ghs.en: Touko: "I do not say 'shan't' you know!!!"

rows.jp: 「そうエクスクラメイションマークを二つセットでばかり使うなよ」
rows.en: “Stop buying your exclamation marks in two-packs.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't just use sets of three exclamation marks!"
ghs.assessment: The source explicitly says she keeps using exclamation marks in pairs of two. The English says sets of three.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Stop using exclamation marks two at a time.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't just use sets of three exclamation marks!"

rows.jp: 「どんな諫(いさ)めかたなのよ！！」

ghs.en: Touko: "What sort of remonstration is that even meant to be!!!"

rows.jp: 「バカにしてんのっ！？　バカにしてるのよね！　バカにしてーーーーーっ！！」
rows.en: “Are you making fun of me?! You are, aren’t you?! You’re making fuuuuun of me!!”

ghs.en: Touko: "You making fun of me?! You making fun of me! YOU MAKING FUUUUUUN!!!"
ghs.assessment: The final repetition still means 'You're making fun of me.' 'YOU MAKING FUUUUUUN' drops the required object and preposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'YOU'RE MAKING FUN OF MEEEE!'

highlights.text: Touko: "You making fun of me?! You making fun of me! YOU MAKING FUUUUUUN!!!"

rows.jp: 「ふつー会話ってのは友好の証じゃないわけ？　あんたのはただバカにする目的でアプローチしてるだけじゃないのよ！」
rows.en: “Isn't normal conversation supposed to be a sign of friendship? You only ever approach me to make fun of me!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Isn't a normal conversation proof of friendship? Aren't you always approaching with the goal of making people look stupid! You're so stupid so how dare you make me look stupid! I can't believe it I don't want to believe it I don't want to be be made to believe it!"

rows.jp: 「おバカなあんたがどうして私をバカにできるの！？　信じられないし信じたくもないし信じさせたくもないわよ！」
rows.en: “And how does an idiot like you get to make fun of me?! I can't believe it, I refuse to believe it, and I won't let you make me believe it!”

rows.jp: うっとりと耳を傾けていると。

ghs.en: Spellbound I lend my ear to listen closely.
ghs.assessment: 'Lend my ear to listen closely' redundantly combines two listening idioms and lacks the comma after the fronted modifier.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As I listen, spellbound,'

highlights.text: Spellbound I lend my ear to listen closely.

ghs.en: Touko's right hand had grown blurry.
ghs.assessment: Her hand blurs from sudden motion in the narrative moment. 'Had grown blurry' makes it an earlier completed visual state rather than rapid movement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Touko's right hand blurred.'

highlights.text: Touko's right hand had grown blurry.

ghs.assessment: The source says he is struck and knocked down. 'Strike-induced fall' replaces the event and victim with a clinical noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The blow knocks me down.'

highlights.text: Strike-induced fall.

rows.jp: 座る者のない机と椅子を巻き込んで、盛大にすっ転んだ。
rows.en: I went down spectacularly, taking an empty desk and chair with me.

ghs.en: A grand, magnificent fall that drags in even unoccupied chairs and desks.
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator tumbles spectacularly, taking desks and chairs with him. The English is a noun fragment whose 'fall' performs the dragging.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I tumble spectacularly, taking empty desks and chairs with me.'

highlights.text: A grand, magnificent fall that drags in even unoccupied chairs and desks.

rows.jp: 「さすがは合戦格闘術ハラキリ拳、隙がない」
rows.en: “That’s the battlefield art of Harakiri Fist for you. Not a single opening.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "As is to be expected of the 『Close Quarters Hand-to-hand Combat Technique * Harakiri Fist』, no openings."

rows.jp: 「だいたい、あんたたちみたいなピッパラリーと私は住む世界が違うの！　私がここにいるのは間違いであんたたちが私のそばにいることも間違いなの！」
rows.en: “I live in a different world from dimbeciles like you! It's a mistake for me to be here, and a mistake for you people to be anywhere near me!”

ghs.en:
Touko: "Besides, pipparly people like you guys should live in a different world from me! Me being here is wrong, and you people being near me is also wrong!"
* Pipparly = Toukese for dullard.

rows.jp: ※ピッパラリー＝冬子語。頭の弱い人たちの意。

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't all those mean the same thing?"

ghs.assessment: るさい is a clipped 'shut up/noisy.' ''addap' is not intelligible English.
ghs.remedy: Use a clipped 'Shaddap!'

highlights.text: Touko: "'addap!"

rows.jp: 「非処女のヒステリーは見にくいばかりだぞ」
rows.en: “A nonvirgin having hysterics is not a pretty sight.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The hysteria of non-virgins is truly a difficult sight!"

ghs.assessment: 顔がひきつった says her face twitched or stiffened. 'Cramped' describes a muscle spasm and is not idiomatic for facial reaction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her face twitched.'

highlights.text: Her face cramped.

rows.jp: 「あ、あ、あ……あんたが……それを……言うわけ？」
rows.en: “Y-you... You of all people... get to say that to me?”

ghs.en: Touko: "Y-, y-, y-... you've really... said... that?"
ghs.assessment: The source incredulously asks whether Taichi, of all people, is saying that to her. 'You've really said that' loses the accusatory contrast between speaker and statement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Y-you... you're the one saying that to me?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Y-, y-, y-... you've really... said... that?"

rows.jp: 耳クソをほじりながらすっとぼける。
rows.en: I played dumb and picked at my ear.

ghs.en: I pick at some earwax while playing dumb.

rows.en: “Bad doesn’t even begin to cover it...”
Her voice sank to a muffled growl.

ghs.en: In a lowering tone of voice.
ghs.assessment: The source specifies a low, muffled voice. 'A lowering tone' describes a changing pitch and omits muffling.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In a low, muffled voice.'

highlights.text: In a lowering tone of voice.

ghs.en: Touko: "That is just... on a dimension of vulgarity that surpasses..."
ghs.assessment: The line says 'crossing far-distant dimensions...' and leads into her command. The English invents a dimension of vulgarity not present in the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Across dimensions vast and distant...'

highlights.text: Touko: "That is just... on a dimension of vulgarity that surpasses..."

rows.jp: ゆっくりと顔をあげて。
「出て行けーーーーーーーっ！！」
めでたく叩き出された。
rows.en: And so I was duly thrown out.

ghs.assessment: The source says he was duly or happily thrown out. 'Oh joyous forceful expulsion' is a subjectless noun phrase and drops the completed action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And with that, I was cheerfully thrown out.'

highlights.text: Oh joyous forceful expulsion.
